newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-BHP Copper to slash costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-BHP Copper to slash costs.

text.p: BHP Copper boss Burgess Winter expects to slash up to ten U.S. cents a pound off production costs at its troubled Magma operations before the middle of next year and anticipates a rapid rise in the global price of copper in the next six months.
Winter, BHP Copper's Executive General Manager, told Reuters the price of copper "should be" around US$1.15 per pound rather than its current range of around 88-89 cents.
He predicted it would rise to well over the US$1.00 level in the next six months on its way to settling around $1.10-1.15.
Magma, the second largest copper producer in the world, was purchased by Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) earlier this year for US$2.4 billion.

It lost money for BHP, one of the largest listed companies in Australia, in the 1996/97 first quarter (June/August) -- a result which shocked the local share market and sent BHP's share price tumbling.
BHP has been badly bruised by the slump in copper prices, stimulated in part by the Sumitomo trading scandal which emerged mid-year and slashed prices by more than 25 per cent.
